The level page is built by `v25Subs('master')`, which gives 7 domains, then The whole paper (not counted), then Tasting, The Floor, Pairing and Service. That makes 11 counted subsections. The card shows the mean of their shares, clamped to 1..99.

**1. Theory: MASTER_QUESTIONS in js/data-master.js** (450 KB, 643 lines, one JSON object per line, under `/* ---- Cat ---- */` blocks)
- There are 576 entries. Every one has `id`, `cat`, `q`, `sa:1`, `accept[]`, `ans` and `exp`. One entry also has `list:1, items[], need`.
- 0 multiple choice, 0 matching, 0 select, 0 `ex` flags.
- 16 per category in 34 categories, 17 in Producers & Icons, 15 in Southern France.
- Ids look like `m-` plus 8 base36 characters, all unique.
- Example: {"id":"m-efo2as8e","cat":"Burgundy","q":"Recite the six grands crus of Vosne-Romanée, in any order.","sa":1,"accept":["~romanee-conti la tache richebourg romanee-saint-vivant la romanee la grande rue"],"ans":"Romanée-Conti, La Tâche, …","exp":"…"}
- In `accept`, `~` means strict whole-phrase matching (core.js:75). A bare number matches a whole number token. `ans` always grades by exact normalised equality (core.js:72).
- The block order in the file is historical: per-country blocks, then themed blocks such as "Vintage command" and "Blind tasting mastery", then "Second pass" blocks. The engine reads only `cat`.

**2. Chapters: MASTER_PRIMERS in js/data-primers-master.js** (40.6 KB)
- 36 objects, one per category, each {cat, lead, exam, facts:[[label,text]×4], traps:[×3]}.
- Example: {cat:"Burgundy", lead:"Burgundy at Master level is recitation under pressure…", exam:"Full grand cru lists, monopole ownership…", facts:[["Recite, don't reconstruct","Gevrey's nine and Vosne's six…"],…], traps:["Confusing Flagey-Échezeaux's two grands crus with Vosne's six.",…]}.
- The Chapter door finds a chapter by `cat`.

**3. The Floor: FLOOR in js/data-floor.js** (`const`, shared by all levels, picked by `lvl`)
- Fields: `id` (f- slug, the key for ST.floor), `lvl`, `s`, `opts[4]`, `best`, `why`.
- 4 entries have lvl 'master', out of 28. Example: id "f-va-over-line", lvl "master", s "A regular orders SP68 from Arianna Occhipinti…".

**4. Pairing: PAIRS in js/data-pairing.js**
- Fields: `id` (p- slug, the key for ST.pairs), `lvl`, `dish`, `needs[]` drawn from the fixed set acid / tannin / low-tannin / sweet / body / low-alc / bubbles / oak / low-oak, `wines[4]`, `best`, `why`.
- 4 entries have lvl 'master', out of 26.

**5. Tasting**
- TASTE in js/data-tasting.js: 47 entries of {g, acid, tan, body, alc, oak (0-3), sweet (0-2), world, clim, age}.

- It has no `lvl` field, and `serviceReadiness()` (codex11.js:95) takes no level argument.
- Progress is ST.serv.svc[partIndex][stepIndex], so it is keyed by position.

**A. A new Grand Cru question** (the main kind)

Standalone:
1. Write a one-line object without `id` in C:/Users/zpull/SommeliersCodex-canon-audit/js/data-master.js. Either append a new `/* ═══════ … ═══════ */` block before the closing `];` (the current last line carries no trailing comma, so add one), or insert it into the category's block.
2. Fields: `"cat"` must be one of the 36 names in core.js `DRILL_GROUPS` exactly. Any other name falls into a "More" domain and changes the level page. Then `"q"`, `"sa":1`, `"accept":[…]` (lower-case, accents folded; `~` for strict phrases), `"ans"`, `"exp"`, and for lists `"list":1,"items":[…],"need":N`.
3. Keep `|` out of stems. No two stems may share their first 80 characters.
4. Update `EXPECT["MASTER_QUESTIONS"]` (576) in .scripts/mint-ids.py:45. Otherwise the dry run reports COUNT MISMATCH. Note that `--apply` still writes despite the mismatch.
5. Run `py .scripts/mint-ids.py` (dry run), then `py .scripts/mint-ids.py --apply`. The id is seeded from json.dumps([cat,q]) and is added only to objects that have none. Never re-mint or strip.
6. Bump `js/data-master.js?v=5` in index.html and `CACHE='codex-v73'` in sw.js. The file is already precached (sw.js:46).
7. Refresh the counts in CLAUDE.md and the HANDOFF.md table. CLAUDE.md still says 489 and 391.

Suite:
1. Write the same object into C:/Users/zpull/OOT-canon-audit/codex/js/data-master.js with the minted `id` copied verbatim from the standalone.
2. Re-word every em dash in the suite's own voice; do not swap characters mechanically.
3. Never mint in the suite. Its re-worded stem would seed a different id.
4. Bump `js/data-master.js?v=7` in codex/index.html and `CACHE='oot-codex-v107'` in codex/sw.js.
5. Commit, then publish through the `_publish` mirror (a plain `git push origin main` there). Do not `git add -A` there before publish.mjs prints its staged-files line.
6. For bulk work, .scripts/canon-audit/apply-edits.cjs takes an optional root as argv[3] and applies exact find/replace jobs, checking that each find appears once and that the JS still parses.

**B. A chapter fact or trap**
- Add `["Label","text"]` to `facts`, or a string to `traps`, of the matching `cat` object in js/data-primers-master.js.
- Make the same change, without em dashes, in codex/js/data-primers-master.js.
- Bump `?v=3` in the standalone and `?v=4` in the suite, plus both CACHE values.
- No content gate reads chapters.

**C. A floor scenario**
- Add `{ id: "f-<slug>", lvl: "master", s, opts:[4], best, why }` to FLOOR in js/data-floor.js. The ids are hand-made, permanent slugs; never renumber.
- The file is byte-identical in both trees: copy it, then bump `data-floor.js?v=1` in both index.html files and both CACHE values.
- The file header's rule applies: four believable options, then a second pass whose job is to refute.

**D. A pairing**
- Add `{ id: "p-<slug>", lvl: "master", dish, needs:[levers from the fixed set], wines:[4], best, why }` to PAIRS in js/data-pairing.js.
- Same two-tree copy and version bumps as C.

**E. A Grand Cru tasting set**
- Today this is impossible without code. `LEVELS.master.grapes` is the Premier Cru list.
- Any new grape needs both a GRAPES_PLUS record with all 8 fields (`st` segments separated by `·`) and a TASTE profile whose `g` matches exactly.
- A separate Grand Cru pool, or origin, appellation or vintage calls in the grid, needs a new layer. By the layer rule that is js/codex27.js, added to index.html, sw.js ASSETS and the check-home FILES list, in both trees.

**F. Service steps**
- Steps can only be appended, at the end of a part's `steps` or as a new part at the end of SERVICE. Progress is keyed by position, so inserting in the middle moves every saved tick.
- Any change alters all four levels.
- SERVICE is in codex6.js, an earlier layer, so a change belongs in a new layer.

**G. A Gauntlet door on the level page** (if wanted)
- Do it in a new layer, codex27.js, that wraps codex25's level page. It must not edit codex25.js.
- `data-go` must resolve through `V25_GO`, or check-home fails.
- Do not restyle anything. Visuals belong to ChatGPT (codex26 and the house*.css files).

map.risks:
1. **Two gates are failing right now.** Any expansion should first triage the 38 new check-paid problems (22 in Master) introduced by 83b705a, either by fixing them or by recording them in rewrite/paid_known.py as a deliberate decision. Otherwise new problems hide among them. list-harness has 3 long-standing Advanced failures that predate this work.

2. **Ids.** Mint only in the standalone and copy the id verbatim to the suite. A stem re-worded for the suite would mint a different id and lose progress. mint-ids `--apply` writes even when the count is wrong, so update EXPECT first and read the dry run.

3. **Two graders.** The suite's core.js has the `saConjHit` rule and the standalone (and rewrite/lib.py) does not. A new accept list must pass sa-harness in the standalone and check-grading.mjs in the suite. The list counts already differ (18 against 20). Use sa-probe.js before widening or narrowing an accept list. A false reject is the worst defect: `ex`-style narrowing once broke 23 correct answers.

4. **Editing `ans` changes list grading.** An item over 40 characters drops the question out of list grading, and a number word in the stem can become `need`. Compare the detected count before and after, not only the pass count.

5. **Dashes.** Standalone text carries em dashes (702 in data-master.js). Copying them into codex/ fails publish.mjs's dash gate. The suite's text has to be re-worded by hand, and CFL voice rules apply.

6. **Shared lists.** FLOOR, PAIRS, TASTE and SERVICE are used by all four levels. A grape or service step added for Grand Cru changes Premier Cru's and Village's Tasting/Service totals and their "met" figures. Service progress is keyed by position, so only append.

7. **Layer discipline and visuals.** New behaviour (a Gauntlet door, a Grand Cru tasting pool, grid origin calls) belongs in codex27.js in both trees. Add it to index.html, sw.js ASSETS and the check-home FILES list, and register any ST store in ST_DEFAULTS and check-merge. The house art (codex26, css/house*.css) is ChatGPT's and must not be restyled. check-home holds the four blurbs and the subsection layout verbatim.

8. **Accuracy.** This content was AI-written in the project; about one claimed error in six was itself wrong. Never change a defensible keyed answer, put nuance in `exp`, and send new material through an examiner pass and then a refute pass (the data-floor.js method).

9. **Trees and branches.** Do not touch C:/Users/zpull/SommeliersCodex (the main checkout holds another author's uncommitted atlas work). Work stays on canon-audit in both worktrees, and shipping waits for the atlas branch. Publish through the `_publish` mirror with a plain push, and clear service workers before checking in a browser (`?nosw` does not stop an installed worker).

10. **Stale documents.** CLAUDE.md (489/391) and HANDOFF.md (codex-v49, "16 Master" list questions) give wrong counts. Run the counts rather than trusting them.

Examples: Sancerre's three soils; Savennières' Coulée de Serrant and Roche aux Moines; the Muscadet crus' lees minimum; the Zotzenberg/Kaefferkopf exceptions; Crémant d'Alsace rosé grape; Bandol's and Cahors' minimums; Limoux's Saint-Hilaire claim and Blanquette against Crémant; Macvin; vin de paille du Jura; Chignin-Bergeron; Sciaccarellu on granite; Côte Brune/Blonde and Côte-Rôtie's Viognier share; Guigal's three LaLas with their slopes; La Place's actors and its non-Bordeaux icons; Cru Bourgeois since 2020; the minor Champagne grapes; Barolo's soil split; Gravner's qvevri; Soave Classico; Bolgheri Sassicaia DOC 2013; Primitivo=Tribidrag (twice); the Gratallops pioneers and llicorella; the Rías Baixas subzones; Bierzo's 2017 ladder; Cava de Paraje; the Douro's subzones, A-to-F grading and beneficio; Colares; talha; Roter Hang; Dönnhoff; the Thermenregion; Bikavér's blend rule; Retsina's resin; Lalou's domaines; Cros Parantoux; Monfortino/Francia; the Paris 1976 winemakers; Konstantin Frank; the Berlin Tasting; Chile's 2011 labelling; the Old Vine Charter's top tier; Waiheke; the MCC rules and name change; VOS/VORS; Eiswein and Icewine law; vin de liqueur against VDN; Cognac's crus; bourbon's pillars; light-strike; keeving; sake class polishing ratios; hiyaoroshi; TDN; Vino de Pago. Plan for expanding Grand Cru (key master) in the Sommelier Codex. Planning only; nothing has been edited. Work happens on canon-audit in C:/Users/zpull/SommeliersCodex-canon-audit (HEAD d289e07) and is ported to C:/Users/zpull/OOT-canon-audit/codex (HEAD 918fb9685). The main checkout C:/Users/zpull/SommeliersCodex is never touched.

The content model is unchanged and no new code layer is needed:
- up to 144 theory questions in data-master.js;
- 72 facts and 36 traps appended to data-primers-master.js;
- 5 Floor scenarios and 5 Pairing dishes appended to the shared data-floor.js and data-pairing.js, which are byte-identical in both trees;
- a first fact check of the 252 existing chapter items.

Two gate steps come first:
- W0 clears check-paid, which is red with 38 new problems (22 in Master) from 83b705a.
- W0b adds a cross-level overlap gate, check-overlap.js. Checks against the real banks showed the original topic list duplicated over 40 Premier Cru stems and several existing Grand Cru stems, and nothing currently stops that.

Theory topics are tagged:
- KEEP: verified absent at both levels;
- CONVERT: Premier Cru asks the fact, so Grand Cru asks the full recitation, the numbers or an argued position;
- REPLACE: the original was a duplicate. A 'gate-check' candidate is provisional until check-overlap.js clears it.

Rules for every new question:
- Recitations use list:1/items/need, never single-word accept entries.
- Stems must read well aloud for codex8's oral mode.
- 144 is a ceiling, not a quota.

Left out on purpose, because each needs a codex27.js layer in both trees and the owner's sign-off: a Grand Cru tasting pool or origin/appellation/vintage calls; a Gauntlet or oral door on the level page; Service grading or Grand Cru service steps. No TASTE or GRAPES_PLUS additions and no restyling.

Expected counts afterwards:
- MASTER_QUESTIONS 576 + N, where N ≤ 144.
- sa-harness master all OK.
- list-harness master detected = 18 + the intended list items.
- check-paid: no new problems, every kept problem justified.
- check-overlap clean.
- check-home 189/189 standalone and 190/190 suite.
- Suite check-grading 1,964 + N, and the suite paraphrase probe agrees with sa-probe on every new id.

workstreams.pipeline:
THE THEORY PIPELINE (W1 to W6 all use it).

1. SELECT:
- Each topic stub goes through check-overlap.js.
- A colliding REPLACE or gate-check item is swapped from the category's pre-checked reserve.
- Shortfalls are recorded, not padded.

2. AUTHOR (one agent per category):
- Write the object without an id: cat, q, sa:1, accept[] (lower-case, accents folded, ~ only on long strict phrases), ans, exp. Recitations use list:1/items/need.
- Write examiner prompts; nuance goes in exp.
- Cite a primary source per claim (INAO/eAmbrosia, TTB, IVDP, the Consejo Regulador, VDP, Wine Australia, SAWIS/WOSA, the NZ GI register, NTA), otherwise the Oxford Companion 5th edition, Wine Grapes or the World Atlas 8th edition.
- No '|' in stems.

3. REFUTE:
- Two refuters with web access quote the source line; an arbiter settles disagreements.
- Superlative, ownership and genetic claims need a dated source.

4. CORRECT:
- Apply confirmed findings only and never change a defensible key.
- An item that cannot be sourced is replaced from the reserve.

5. CRITIC (text pass):
- Grand Cru need, ambiguity, recitable in under a minute.
- Reads aloud: no slashes, bracketed asides or abbreviations in q.
- Rerun check-overlap.

6. MINT:
- Update EXPECT['MASTER_QUESTIONS'] in .scripts/mint-ids.py.
- Clean dry run, then --apply once. Never re-mint.

7. PROBE:
- sa-probe.js by id with 3 right paraphrases and 2 near misses. A false reject is a blocker.
- Accept-list fixes after minting keep the id.

8. GATES:
- check-syntax.
- sa-harness master: 0 WRONG, 0 unsure.
- list-harness: detected count rises by exactly the intended list items, all at full marks.
- check-claims: 0 failures; read the new lint lines.
- check-paid in the background: new cross_accept lines are fixed or given a written decision.
- check-overlap.
- check-home 189/189.

9. SUITE PORT (W11), then commit both trees.
workstreams.whyItMatters: The real French gaps are full recitations: Chablis, the Montrachets, Margaux's thirds, the second wines, the seventeen villages and crus, the Savoie and Corsica crus. Rule sets such as Quarts de Chaume Grand Cru, the VT/SGN numbers and Graves 1959 are gaps too. The facts Premier Cru already asks are not.

The critic recomputes every worked figure, and accept lists take the number with and without the currency or unit.
workstreams.whyItMatters: The Craft is where floor work meets theory. The gaps are fault chemistry, legal limits, oak and maceration, large formats, the iron and sauce mechanisms, valuation and truth in menu. TDN, US label percentages and BTG maths are already held.

workstreams.name: W7 Chapters: two facts and one trap per Grand Cru chapter
workstreams.target: Standalone: js/data-primers-master.js, appending [label,text] to facts and a string to traps of each cat object. Nothing existing is replaced, and labels are not repeated. Suite: codex/js/data-primers-master.js, re-worded without em dashes.
topics: Every chapter: fact 1 condenses the category's new, refuted recitations, and fact 2 the mechanism or law. The trap is the commonest wrong answer refuters met.
Labels are written only after the revised questions clear refutation. The original label list is discarded because it names dropped topics.
Wine Fundamentals: keep all four oral-technique facts and three traps. Append 'Reduction chemistry' and 'Faults in numbers', plus a trap on 4-EP against 4-EG.
Facts run about 250 to 400 characters, bringing chapters toward Premier Cru's 6 facts and 4 traps.
Every new fact passes check-overlap primer mode against ADV_PRIMERS and MASTER_PRIMERS.
workstreams.pipeline:
1. AUTHOR after the category's questions pass refutation.
2. REFUTE against the corrected questions' sources.
3. CORRECT.
4. CRITIC reads the whole chapter for contradiction, repetition and level fit.
5. GATES: check-syntax; check-overlap primer mode; check-home; a Chapter door read in the browser with service workers cleared. check-primer-similarity.py does not apply.
6. SUITE: re-word without em dashes; the dash gate stays at baseline.
workstreams.whyItMatters: Grand Cru chapters are about two-thirds of Premier Cru's. A chapter must teach what the new questions test without losing the oral technique the level is built on.

workstreams.name: W8 Chapter audit: first fact check of the existing Grand Cru chapters
workstreams.target: Standalone: js/data-primers-master.js, the 144 existing facts and 108 traps, edited in place only on confirmed error. Suite: codex/js/data-primers-master.js, which already differs on 54 lines, so corrections are made by meaning.
topics: Every existing fact and trap, checked claim by claim against a source.
Priority 1: numbers and dates.
Priority 2: ownership and first/only/largest claims.
Priority 3: contradictions with the 205 canon-audited questions' corrected ans or exp.
Keep a claim-to-line map for both trees.
workstreams.pipeline:
1. AUDIT: one auditor per domain gives a verdict and source per claim.
2. REFUTE every 'wrong' verdict.
3. CORRECT confirmed claims only, keeping labels.
4. CRITIC reads each changed chapter whole.
5. GATES: check-syntax, check-home, a Chapter door read; diff the claim map across trees.
6. SUITE: port by meaning, no em dashes.
Runs alongside W1 to W6.
workstreams.whyItMatters: No gate reads chapters, and the canon audit changed 205 questions without re-reading them, so a chapter may now teach what the bank marks wrong.

workstreams.name: W9 The Floor: five Grand Cru scenarios
workstreams.target: js/data-floor.js FLOOR, byte-identical in both trees: append { id:'f-<slug>', lvl:'master', s, opts:[4], best (index), why }. Ids are permanent. Bump data-floor.js?v= in both index.html files at release.
topics: f-wrong-bottle-opened: a junior opens a four-figure Burgundy for the wrong table. Own it at the house's cost, salvage the bottle, coach after service. Pitched on ownership, unlike f-wrong-vintage-up.

f-fining-allergy: a guest with a severe egg or fish allergy asks about fining you cannot confirm for that bottle. Steer to verifiable wines. Check against retained Reg 1169/2011 and 579/2012 and the Food Information Regulations 2014.

f-list-price-typo: the printed list shows a first growth at a tenth of its price. Decide the house's response and the words at the table. Distinct from f-price-dispute. Check against UK pricing law (CPUT/CRA 2015).

f-suspect-carry-in (replaces f-sediment-on-demand): a regular brings a famous old bottle for corkage, and the capsule, label and fill look wrong; the table is celebrating. Distinct from f-cloudy-carry-in.
f-menu-changed-after-pairing: at 6 pm the kitchen swaps a sauce after the pairing is printed and the wines pulled. Re-pair, brief the floor, tell the guests.
workstreams.pipeline:
Follow the data-floor.js header method.
1. AUTHOR: four believable options with no straw men; why also explains the nearest miss; money in pounds.
2. REFUTE: two refuters argue for another option and check every legal or allergen claim against UK sources. If a refuter wins, rewrite.
3. CORRECT.
4. CRITIC: the owner's three-star floor read, and distinct from every existing scenario at every level.
5. GATES: check-syntax in both trees; check-home; in the browser with service workers cleared, the Floor drill deals 8 and the Finals 6 from the master pool, and the count line no longer widens; check-merge unchanged.
6. Copy byte for byte to the suite; keep it free of em dashes.
workstreams.whyItMatters: Grand Cru has 4 scenarios against Premier Cru's 9. The drill asks for 8 and the test for 6, and at 4 the level sits on byLevel's threshold.

workstreams.name: W10 Pairing: five Grand Cru dishes
workstreams.target: js/data-pairing.js PAIRS, byte-identical in both trees: append { id:'p-<slug>', lvl:'master', dish, needs:[from acid, tannin, low-tannin, sweet, body, low-alc, bubbles, oak, low-oak], wines:[4], best (index), why }. Bump data-pairing.js?v= in both index.html files at release.
topics: p-ris-de-veau-morilles (replaces p-poulet-vin-jaune-morilles): veal sweetbreads, morels, Madeira cream. needs acid, body, low-tannin. Best is not Jura; set it against mature white Burgundy, aged Savennières and a red Burgundy premier cru.
p-pigeon-salmis: roast pigeon with a blood-and-liver salmis. needs tannin, acid, body.
p-oursin-raw: raw sea urchin on toasted brioche. needs acid, low-oak, bubbles; why carries the iron and iodine logic.
p-peking-duck: pancakes, hoisin, cucumber, spring onion. needs low-tannin, acid, sweet.
p-tarte-tatin-creme-fraiche: needs sweet, acid. A sweet Chenin as best, against Sauternes, Tokaji and Moscato d'Asti.
workstreams.pipeline:
1. AUTHOR:
- levers only from the fixed set;
- four real wines;
- best and why argued on mechanism.
Rules: no dish is cooked in its own best wine, and no best repeats a region already used as best at Grand Cru (Chablis, Jura, Mosel).
2. REFUTE: two refuters each argue for a rejected wine; check each dish against Escoffier or Larousse Gastronomique.
3. CORRECT.
4. CRITIC: would a Master examiner accept the best without argument?
5. GATES: check-syntax in both trees; check-home; the Pairing drill deals 6 from the master pool; check-merge unchanged.
6. Copy byte for byte to the suite.
workstreams.whyItMatters: Grand Cru has 4 dishes against Premier Cru's 9, and the drill asks for 6. Today's set has no classical sauce, no game with blood, no raw shellfish and no dessert.

workstreams.name: W11 Suite port, gates and ship
workstreams.target: Standalone C:/Users/zpull/SommeliersCodex-canon-audit and suite C:/Users/zpull/OOT-canon-audit/codex, both on canon-audit, then the OutsideOfTime/_publish mirror.
topics: Port each wave's questions with ids copied verbatim (never mint in the suite), and the chapter items, re-worded by hand without em dashes in the CFL voice.
Build a scratch suite paraphrase probe from codex/js core.js, codex8 and codex9 (with saConjHit). Its verdicts must match the standalone sa-probe on every new id.

At ship: fetch, check status, rebase onto the landed atlas work, then read ?v= (data-master, data-primers-master, data-floor, data-pairing) and CACHE in both trees and bump once. If canon-audit has not shipped, ship both under one bump.
Refresh CLAUDE.md (489/391) and HANDOFF.md (codex-v49, '16 Master') from fresh counts.

Full gate run recorded in the commit message: mint-ids, sa-harness, list-harness, check-claims, check-paid, check-overlap, check-home 189/190, check-merge, check-syntax, check-grading.mjs, the suite probe, the publish dash gate.
Publish through the _publish mirror with a plain git push origin main. Never git add -A there before publish.mjs prints its staged-files line. Clear service workers, then run qidAudit().
workstreams.whyItMatters: The level only improves when both trees carry it and the service worker serves it. The trees use different graders and wording, so a port is a gated step, not a copy.

plan.order:
1. W0 first, alone. check-paid must print 'no new problems', the baseline is re-recorded only after every keep-decision is written, the baseline counts are recorded, and both trees are committed.

2. W0b next. Build and calibrate check-overlap.js and commit it. No topic is authored before it exists.

3. Then three things in parallel:
- The theory waves W1 to W6 in domain order. Each wave runs: select through check-overlap; author; two refuters plus an arbiter; correct; critic text and oral pass; update EXPECT; mint dry run then --apply once; sa-probe by id; gates (check-paid in the background). Then its W11 port with the suite paraphrase probe, and a commit in both trees before the next wave mints.
- W8, the chapter audit.
- W9 Floor and W10 Pairing (any time after W0).

4. W7 chapters per category, after that category's questions pass refutation. Labels come from the revised topics, and Wine Fundamentals keeps its oral facts.

5. Release (W11). Wait for the atlas branch. Fetch and rebase, read ?v= and CACHE fresh in both trees and bump once (together with canon-audit if it has not shipped). Refresh the CLAUDE.md and HANDOFF.md counts. Publish through the _publish mirror with a plain push, clear service workers and run qidAudit().

Out of scope until the owner decides, because each needs a codex27.js layer in both trees: a Grand Cru tasting pool or origin/appellation/vintage calls; a Gauntlet or oral door on the level page; Service grading or Grand Cru service steps.
